title.narrative: Promoting resource smart green technologies in technical professional and higher education to increase Mozambique's food production and nutrition security

description.narrative:
The proposed project must contribute to the following ++objective++:
- End hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture (SDG 2)
The proposed project must contribute to the following ++long-term impacts++:
- Promote agricultural growth; - Reduce malnutrition; and - Create ecologically sustainable food systems.
The ++medium-term impacts++ that will contribute to this:
1. Education system (TVET/HE) is of good quality, relevant and accessible (SDG 4); 2. Partnerships between persons and organisations are inclusive and sustainable (SDG 17); 3. Organizations key to (sectoral) inclusive development of partner countries are strengthened by inflow of enhanced workforce.
++Outcome++:
HE (Higher Education) and TVET (Technical Colleges) organisations (in Mozambique and in NL) perform better their core tasks, and are firmly embedded in their environment (in line with specific labour market needs & aiming at inclusiveness).
To that end, the following ++outputs ++must be achieved by the end of the project:
1. Enhanced institutional capacity through hands-on training of teachers, technicians, researchers and students; 2. Increase the quality of agricultural educational programs in Mozambique with an emphasis on hands-on training, inclusiveness & gender, (food) system approach, resilience to climate change, entrepreneurship, and private sector involvement and at the same time enhance collaboration between agricultural research (research institution), Polytechnic education and TVET education to complement each other and share best practices; 3. Established and sustained Centre for Innovation and Resource-Smart Green Technologies adapted to the local context and addressing different needs of the agricultural sector.
​

comment.narrative: 16-09-2023: Short training modules on: - Greenhouse production - Open field production - Career Development (action plan proposal created per institution) - Quality Assurance for Higher education, main challenges in Mozambique

30-06-2021: The MSc program has been newly developed with the support from Polytechnic Institute of Bragança (IPB) University of Lisbon, School of Agriculture (ISA). the activity started October 2020 with two groups, one in Portugal (ISA and IPB) and other in Mozambique. The results of the LMNA were studied. The area linked with environment and technological engineering and technology environment was a highlight, and at the end, the MSc proposed is in “Environmental management and sustainable development”. Next step is to submit the proposal to the National Council for Quality Evaluation (Ministry of Education in Mozambique) for a pre-approvement to start the activities. The process can take a year, so the expectation would be to start in 2022.

title.narrative: A.E.3. Number of staff that have gained qualitative and relevant knowledge and skills to develop and offer the revised/developed study programmes

comment.narrative: 04-01-2022: The capacity development activities have involved a number of staff from the partner organizations: 7 directly in the training for labor market assessment, 6 in the gender assessment, and 2 female administrative staff have benefited from public relations training. Due to the restrictions for mobility and gathering it was not possible to include more people during 2020, but the numbers can be easily reached during 2021, taking into account the activities still planned. 2 PhD students have been also supported with the project.

16-09-2023: A number of training activities took place during 2022 and 2023. These trainings were:
2022 - Didactic training for TVET( 31) - Regenerative Agriculture(21) - Project proposal (109) - Gender and leadership (33) - Exposure visit to the Netherlands (8)
2023 - Introduction to Didactics in Higher Education (27) - Radio broadcasting (rules and management) (12) - Career Development (28) - Quality Assurance for Higher Education (26) - Basic journalism (16) - Event: Gender and inclusiveness, participative methods for higher education (103) - Greenhouses management (40) - Lead Farmers (93) - Social media, radio content creation and radio station management (16).
Some of the staff/teachers participated in more than one or several of these training sessions. The PhD students (2) continued with their activities. One of the them has finished the thesis and defense is planned for September 2023. The other students will finish in December 2024.

title.narrative: A.S.1. Number of beneficiaries in the society reached with knowledge, skills and techniques

comment.narrative: 16-09-2023: 50 farmers directly contacted with the visits during the training lead farmers, 75.000 directly reached with the radio and informative programmes. The radio reaches all districts of Manica province and two districts in Sofala province. This means that more than 500 000 people are reached directly. Counting only 15% of the total population, it is possible to calculate 75.000.

25-06-2021: Community was not been reached yet due to the mobility and gathering restrictions during 2020. Work has concentrated in the partners of the consortium. It will be possible once situation is normal to reach populations. The implementation of the investment and the construction of the Centre for Innovation and Resource-Smart Green Technologies will facilitate the contact with farmers and the training.

comment.narrative: 25-06-2021: Investment plan for the ISPM, IAC and IIAM is in place now, as part of the business plan development for the Resource centers. Implementation will take place in year 2.

title.narrative: A.E.1. Number of (knowledge) institutions supported directly

comment.narrative: 25-06-2021: The activities developed have involved staff from the 3 organizations making part of the project: Instituto Superior Politécnico de Manica (ISPM), Instituto de investigação Agrária de Moçambique (IIAM) and Instituto Médio Técnico-Profissional Agrário de Chimoio (IMTPAC).
26-09-2023: During this period, the three partner institutions of the project have been supported directly: ISPM, IAC and IIAM

title.narrative: A.O.2. Number of organisations revised/developed and implemented a strategic plan

comment.narrative: 25-06-2021: The focus in this project was the development of strategic/business plans for the resource centers and not focus on the total organization, because that is out of the scope of the project. The plans for ISPM, IAC and IIAM are available now for further implementation.

title.narrative: A.R.2. Number of relevant publications (level, gender, inclusion)

comment.narrative:
16-09-2023: Two lecturers from ISPM have presented their research at the 60-year celebration of Higher Education in Mozambique and Angola. The debates included topics on the differentiation and typology of higher education institutions towards their consolidation and transformation taking into consideration aspects related to sustainability, including the role of the policies of higher education, the place of scientific research, extension and innovation in the training of students and the qualification of teachers, in a context marked by quality demands, relevance and employability of the students and internationalization. A lecturer from ISPM and Teresa Patatas, from Escola Superior Politénica do Namibe in Angola reflected of the topic: 60 anos de ensino superior em Angola e Moçambique: reflexão sobre a participação dos dois países no fórum de gestão de ensino superior nos países e regiões da língua portuguesa (60 Years of higher education in Angola and Mozambique: reflections on the participation of the two countries in forum for the management of higher education in Portuguese speaking countries and regions). One of the PhD trainees, shared the experience of ISPM during the pandemic through the presentation: Impacto da COVID-19 no processo de treinamento de futuros rangers florestais: um caso do curso de ecoturismo e gestão de fauna bravia no Instituto Superior Politécnico de Manica (ISPM), Moçambique (Impact of the COVID -19 in training forest rangers: Case study of the undergraduate degree in eco-tourism and wildlife management at Instituto Superior Politécnico de Manica (ISPM), Mozambique.
PhD candidate and ISPM lecturer article “Hydroelectricity and Biomass use in Mozambique, an Overview”, will be published in the Journal of Environmental Protection (JEP).

25-06-2021: The following documents are done: • Labour market assessment: the Inventory of needs (training) Co-created with the technicians and researchers of the institutes. • Gender need assessment report of ISPM, IIAM and IMTPAC
There was an e-learning scan assessment but the Incubator assessment was postponed for 2021.

title.narrative: A.S.2. Number of MoUs or other types of collaboration agreements signed (education, private, public, surrounding community)

comment.narrative: 16-09-2023: Collaboration agreement between ISPM and WFP to support the implantation of three projects and conduct studies in central and southern Mozambique. Collaboration agreement between IAC, IIAM, ISPM and Business Council to create a virtual reference centre and promote innovation in agriculture. Collaboration agreement with CEFA, Italian NGO to submit a joint application aiming at supporting women to the Italian agency for international development. Collaboration agreement between ISPM and MCTES to support the implementation of three capacity-building projects at ISPM. Collaboration agreement with Provincial Council to prevent HIV –AIDS in Manica Province. Collaboration agreement with UNIDO to support installation of seedbank of tropical fruit crops at ISPM.

25-06-2021: There are MOU’s with many organizations to provide workplace training.
In Mozambique, ISPM has signed collaboration agreement with IIAM and IMTPAC. Additional collaboration agreements signed include: a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between ISPM and ETG for the productions of different agricultural crops within ISPM production unit, which will contribute to operationalise the Centre for Innovation and Resource-Smart Green Technologies. A Momorandum of Understanding between ISPM and FSDMoç for the provision of financial services, which will increase the capacity of the ISPM incubation center to provide services to the community, to promote self-employment and entrepreneurship. Moreover, ISPM and Lúrio University (UniLurio) have agreed to expand their existing collaboration into other areas, which would enable the involvement of Lúrio University in activities of the project OKP-MOZ-104294, particularly in aspects regarding pilot testing and demonstrations of the innovations. In order to operationalise this, ISPM and Lúrio University will sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU).

title.narrative: A.E.4. Number of graduates delivered

comment.narrative: 16-09-2023: During this period there were 154 graduates who followed improved courses and methodologies In terms of minorities, approximately 16% (25 students) of the ISPM students come from rural and remote areas. Hence, they are relatively disadvantaged and can also be considered minorities. In addition to those, in 2022 ISPM provided the support and contributed to the graduation of one blind student. This was a learning experience showing that it was possible to adapt creating the required support for students with these limitations.

title.narrative: A.S.3. Number of students performing an internship or practical work

comment.narrative: 16-09-2023: Students of the seven undergraduate programmes at ISPM have participated internships with private companies.

title.narrative: A.E.6. Number of students enrolled in revised/newly developed study programmes

comment.narrative: 16-09-2023: There have been 241 new enrolments at ISPM in 2023. All students will be trained using revised curricula and novel teaching approaches, and using the new infrastructure (greenhouses, laboratory equipment, etc). As for the farmers, enrolments are based on demand. However, the ISPM signed an agreement with the Technical and Vocational training Authority to provide training of trainers (ToTs) for seventeen (17) teachers of TVETs in aspects related to Mechanization and use of Agricultural Equipment

title.narrative: A.S.4. Number of SMEs supported

comment.narrative: 16-09-2023: It was not possible to register this indicator within the strict time of the project. This is because the greenhouses were important to be able to develop the majority of the low-tech inputs and these were finished during 2023. However, the partners are already working in a plan to deliver these inputs and it will be finished very soon this year. On the other hand, the revolving fund was identified as the best sustainable manner to support the work that the Business Incubation Centre is doing. Its establishment with clear rules and working formats will allow a transparent, replicable and long-term environmental, social, and economic impact. Staff from ISPM has been working in coordination with MSM and Q-Point to determine strong governance and terms. This revolving fund (with € 50.000) includes also the use of greenhouses and will be able to fund the scaling production of the inputs from the applied research. ISPM has a plan to accompany the students in the development of their business ideas around known value chains minimising risks.

title.narrative: A.O.11. Number of organisations with policies and procedures to ensure an environment which is gender sensitive

comment.narrative: 16-09-2023: All partners continued working with events and procedures to ensure a gender-sensitive environment. The events in 2023 were very relevant and gathered many other stakeholders working on this topic in the region.

title.narrative: A.R.3. Number of relevant innovations

comment.narrative: 16-09-2023: Although these are still in the face of final trials and experimentation, the researchers and teachers from the local partners have been working on several solutions that will bring innovation to the practices of regional farmers. More time is required to be able to make these fully innovative practices incorporated into the production habits. 1. A novel combination of aquaculture and vegetable production is under development at ISPM facilities whereby the outflux of water from the fishponds are reused to irrigate vegetable plots. 2. Furthermore, ISPM has been promoting syntrophic agriculture as new method of production to local communities in Manica province. This new method gives an additional emphasis in the processes and relationship between plants, soil and the surrounding environment. This will result in a decreased use of external inputs. 3. Researchers at IIAM have been increasing the production of basic seed of improved varieties of maze and legumes to facilitates access to small-scale farmers. 4. Teachers from IAC have been exploring new formulations of food, including enriched and fortified porridge, which includes sweet potato, yam, and banana, as ingredients to decrease malnutrition in children under five-year-old; and 5. Alternative ways to increase the shelf-life of vegetable crops using solar driers.
